thread:
lina: noticing spike in GPU join failures in eu-west-2 since 08:12, warm pool nodes stuck at provisioning
ashok: seeing same, keystore decrypt 403s and auditshipper failing to POST, suspicious egress block
ryan: @lina any recent firewall or natgw changes?
sam: I merged a default-deny rule for outbound in the eu-prod subnet last night (PR #4237) — intended to tighten egress to approved endpoints
ashok: that matches — keystore egress goes to keystore-eu.internal:443 and auditshipper -> logs-usw3.internal:9411, both are being dropped
lina: result = GPU nodes can't fetch instance secrets, kubelet can't start containerd, warm pool stays empty. impacting onboarding and burst capacity
sre-oncall: tagging incident, creating ticket INF-9876. Can we temporarily allow specific egress to unblock? :hourglass_flowing_sand:
ryan: yes, need short-term exception for 172.31.0.0/16 -> keystore-eu.internal:443 and logs endpoints. Prefer security group rule over turning off default-deny
sam: agree, patching SG whitelists now. applying a scoped rule with 1-hr TTL and annotation.
deploy-bot: started apply for terraform module vpc-egress-sg (plan id tf-2026-05-02-08:30)
ashok: while patching, let's also validate KMS grants — some nodes show decrypt errors originating from stale grant tokens
ashok: run: `kubectl logs -n keystore keystore-proxy-0 | grep "decrypt failed"` -> shows sts deny for role arn:aws:iam::...:role/gpu-warmup
ryan: looks like IAM condition `aws:SourceVpc` was tightened too — nodes launched in new warmpool-subnet don't match allowed VPC tag
sam: Ugh. That was from the conditional-authz rollout. I'll revert the condition for the warmup role and add a scoped exception for the warmpool-subnet id: subnet-0a1b2c3d
lina: good. Can we also backfill flow logs for the window (08:00-08:30) so security/audit has the evidence?
sre-oncall: Requesting flowlog quick export to s3://ops-audit/tmp/6509876543. Kickoff now.
ashok: mitigation checklist: 1) add SG egress allow to keystore/logs, 2) relax IAM condition for warmup role, 3) restart warm pool agent on affected nodes, 4) monitor joins
ryan: cost note — keeping broad outbound open increases audit ingestion and egress cost at scale. prefer short TTL + canary then full policy review
sam: PR up: `gitlab.com/redwood/infrarc/merge_requests/789` — description: scoped egress exception + IAM condition exception for warmpool.
ashok: running node-restart job: `./scripts/warmpool-restart.sh --region eu-west-2 --nodes 12`
lina: monitoring dashboard: https://console.redwood.internal/dashboards/warmpool-joins — joins rate climbing from 0 -> 8 in last 4m
sre-oncall: postmortem notes: dependency mapping mismatch between conditional IAM rollout and new subnet naming caused implicit deny. Add to postmortem: map of roles -> allowed subnets.
ryan: next steps after stabilize: 1) automate egress exceptions via ephemeral allowlist, 2) preflight for IAM conditional changes (test overlay), 3) alert if warm pool join rate < threshold for 5m
sam: rollout complete, removing temporary SG exception in 1hr, will close INF-9876 after verification
lina: thanks team, ping me if joins regress. filing follow-up doc in #eng-platform-runbooks
file_description: Slack thread about GPU warm pool onboarding failures caused by VPC egress default-deny and IAM conditional authz; mitigation, short-term SG exception, IAM rollback, runbook and cost discussion.
